rounds.proof_sketch: For fixed shape [16, 16384], size = 262144. Since size >= 4096 and size % 4 == 0, vectorized path is taken. vectorized_grid = (262144/4 + 256 - 1) / 256 = 65791 / 256 = 256 (integer division). With max_blocks = 256, the comparison 'vectorized_grid > max_blocks' (256 > 256 = false → keep 256) vs 'vectorized_grid >= max_blocks' (256 >= 256 = true → set to 256) both produce 256. The mutation is semantically equivalent for this fixed shape.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the grid-size clamping condition from `>` to `>=`. For the fixed input shape [16, 16384] with 262,144 elements, the vectorized_grid computes to exactly 256, which equals max_blocks. When vectorized_grid == max_blocks, the original code evaluates (256 > 256) = false and keeps vectorized_grid = 256, while the mutated code evaluates (256 >= 256) = true and assigns max_blocks = 256. Both produce identical grid sizes (256). Since grid size depends solely on tensor dimensions (not values), and the fixed shape produces this exact boundary case where both operators yield the same result, no value-level test can distinguish the mutant.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation affects grid launch parameters, which are determined solely by tensor dimensions. For the fixed size of 262,144 elements, vectorized_grid equals max_blocks (both 256), making the > vs >= comparison irrelevant since both paths produce 256. To kill this mutant would require changing tensor dimensions to a size where vectorized_grid < max_blocks, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing relational operator mutations on configuration/launch parameters (not data-dependent computations), recognize that fixed-shape contracts can make boundary-case mutations equivalent. Consider adding shape-parameterized tests as a separate test track, or document when mutations are provably equivalent for specific configurations to avoid false survival reports.
